title: Self-Control and Mutual Love
english: While it is permitted to eat meat and drink wine, the authority in these things is not entirely without restriction.
Abstaining from such things is also beneficial, so that we do not harden our flesh through indulgence and make the passions within it wild.
If we abstain from these things for their own sake, we do so much more for the sake of our brother, lest he be hindered by what is said, 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself'.
Therefore, accept one another, as Christ also accepted us into the glory of God.
We, the many, are one body, and members one of another according to what is written, being joined together into the unity of Christ by the bonds of love.
For He Himself who made both one and broke down the middle wall of the fence, abolishing the law of commandments in decrees.
It is therefore necessary to think the same thing toward one another, and if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; if one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
Unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
translator_notes: The Greek text ends mid-word, indicating a cut sentence end.
The phrase 'abolishing in dogmas' is a textual variant.
The verse reference for 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself' is Leviticus 19:18.
The phrase 'the middle of the wall' is a reference to Ephesians 2:14, describing Christ as the one who breaks down the dividing wall.
